rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: body-view grep `em_dash` 0 hits (planted_proof CLEAN), `banned_words` (delve/honest/importantly/crucial/substrate/synergize/paradigm shift) 0 hits (CLEAN), `leverage_verb` 0 hits (CLEAN). No em-dash, no banned word anywhere in body (L1-83).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: body-view grep `ritual_ceremony` 0 hits (planted_proof CLEAN). Body uses "exercise" correctly (L80: "the exercise is already fixing bugs") — the sanctioned replacement word, not the banned ones. No noun-form "practice" anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: body-view grep `dated_line` and `session_biography` both 0 hits in body (L1-83). Re-checked against the 2026-09-05 "chasing phantoms" addition specifically on the maintainer block's L86 note ("Prework owes no licence check and no network/proxy check"): this is a present-tense negative definition, but it names a concrete, real predecessor (`cohort-onboarding-email.md`, which genuinely carried these two checks before being collapsed into this page) — a named live pull a future consolidation pass would plausibly re-propose, not an invented phantom. It is also already listed as a dated accept-note (Antti 2026-08-13) in the body-view's accept_notes. L88's note ("the two {{prompt:}} fences... are accepted, not an unextracted exercise") passes the same test even more clearly: `check_pedagogy.md §52a`'s own grep is the named live puller that would re-flag this section every pass without the note. Neither trips the ban on journey-narration: both state a standing constraint with the historical clause serving as the "empirical finding that would otherwise be re-derived," not a changelog of the edit just made.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read against the AE101 voice quintet: body stays Boris-flat/factual throughout (mechanical setup prose — repo pick, session open, download, extract, bug screen), with Godin warmth surfacing at low-stakes moments (L70 "Small steer, small trick. A minute here, another there." passes the Godin-plausibility test: mischievous+warm, doesn't dunk on student or agent, meaning doesn't flip if misread). No `**Remember:**`/`Hold onto`/`Keep in mind` poster-wrapper grep hits. No cargo/theatre/ritual/tourist/poster valence words. No atmospheric (sensory/time-of-day/body-state/cosmic) imagery to mis-hit a wrong feeling note — prose stays literal throughout, which is the correct default for a setup beat. No negation-callout ("we don't X" / "we refuse Y") present to check for self-contradiction. Audience-caution flinch-greps (`just a simple`, `trust the agent`, leash/niceness metaphors) all absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Credit original when paraphrasing named technique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No named practitioner/technique/framework paraphrased in body (only the Willison pre-read, credited by name inline at L76 — compliant, and pre-reads are exempt from the attribution cap regardless per rule 11). Creator-name grep: "Antti" appears only below the maintainer cut (L86, L88 — explicitly unrestricted there); 0 hits in body. Author-we grep (`author_we` pattern) 0 hits. Belief-by-name: no belief references present, N/A. Timing-by-surface: prework carries NO "**Time:**" line in body (correct — the rule lists prework explicitly among surfaces that must not show timing in body) and instead states "**Runtime:** 30 min target" below the maintainer cut (L101) — exactly the required placement.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Always "you", never "the student"; teacher framing stays out of body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: body-view grep `the_student` 0 hits. Body addresses the reader as "you" throughout (L3 "when you open a session", L26 "which repo are you going to grow", L58-62 bug-screen instructions all second-person). No delivery-mechanics narration ("the trainer shows...", "before students start...") anywhere above the cut.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer-only vocabulary (self-compound, substrate, three-pattern, grill-me, "artefact contracts") does not leak into body. Body describes the same content in plain operational language (e.g. "the AE101 content bundle" not "artefact contract"; "the curated skills" not "self-compound").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Over-hedge detector.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No reassurance-shaped sentences found (no "no penalty", "fine way to", "it's OK if", "not a downgrade", "you are not on the hook for X"). L80's closing "Your call." follows a stated real consequence (scrambling for a bug while the exercise is already running) rather than softening an already-complete delegation sentence, so it reads as genuine agency-framing, not absolution-after-the-fact.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only one practitioner named in body: Willison at L76, and that mention is a pre-read citation — exempt from the cap by the rule's own "prereads and links don't count" carve-out. Well under any cap either way.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No flag phrases present ("not an aspirational X", "not a vendor Y", "grounded in actual", "not theoretical", "from the person running it"). "Vendor" does not appear in body at all. Prework is pure logistics/setup, no positioning language of any kind.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses several Claude Code operational primitives without a one-breath primer: `/model` (L3), thinking-effort levels "high"/"xhigh"/"medium" (L5), the **Session** widget (L38), "Plan mode" (L16), "the AskUserQuestion tool" (L66, L68). All are treated identically — none earned, none primed — which reads as a deliberate, consistent choice: prework establishes baseline platform-operational vocabulary the audience (professional engineers already handed Claude Code for this training) is assumed to already carry, distinct from curriculum-taught concepts under active pedagogical construction elsewhere in the arc (the M3 module "plan-mode-done-right" teaches plan mode as a *skill*, not as a *word*). Because the pattern is consistent across five different terms rather than an isolated slip, I read this as the assumed-known carve-out applied to platform primitives, not a jargon-planting violation.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If the maintainer disagrees that "Plan mode" is assumed-known at this arc position, the fix is a two-word gloss at L16 ("Plan mode — Claude Code's upfront-planning mode — wants...") rather than pulling the reference, since M3 needs the sizing distinction to already exist by the time it teaches the mode properly.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function; pronoun/metaphor-referent check on any closer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every section closer for dangling pronouns/demonstratives and vague spatial/temporal metaphors standing in for an action: L34 "grow that" → repo just built, unambiguous; L70 "A minute here, another there" is a reflective coda (not an instruction with a hidden referent); L80 "you'll be scrambling for one" / L82 "Bring one" → both resolve cleanly to "a trivial bug" from the immediately preceding sentence. No closer requires a hunt to resolve.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only human→agent interaction verbs used are "ask" and "push back" (L45, L62, L66) — both on the peer-flat/warmer list, not the combative list (bark/order/command/whip/force/drag/push around/boss/shout at/snap at/lecture/scold). No carve-out needed; nothing borderline.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No header uses a spatial/structural metaphor that could contradict a mechanism, and none uses "other X" / "the rest of X" without a named primary. All eight headers (Bring real work / Pick THE repo / Open a Claude Code session / Get the content folder / Extract the bundle / Pick a trivial bug / Pre-read before Module 1 / Bring to Module 1) survive a literal cold read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negation ("X, not Y" against a prior no reader held), no deictic drumroll ("That is the X."/"This is the Y."), no bold-label echo (the bullet format at L15-18 is label-colon-description, e.g. "**Trivial bug**, wanted on day one: a few lines..." — a definition-list shape, never restated as the following sentence's subject), no citation/appendix duplication.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L11 already avoids the count ("different task sizes," not "four task sizes") against the four bullets below it. L13's lede "Roughly in the order you'll reach for them" states ordering once; of the four bullets only L15's "wanted on day one" repeats a positional-feeling marker, and it passes the survivor test because it names a real constraint (a deadline — must be picked before arrival), not a bare position. The other three bullets (multi-file task / small feature / bigger piece) carry no redundant positional marker.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No abstract-twin pairs (two sentences at different altitudes stating one idea), no widening qualifiers ("or rule", "or context-dependent"), no second announcement of the same claim elsewhere in the file. The lead-ins preceding each `{{prompt:}}` marker stay at the single required semantic-summary sentence (prompts §2) without adding a restating second sentence — L51-53's permission-mechanics paragraph is new information (why permission prompts fire), not a restatement of the fence below it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap phrasing ("you already think you're using X", "you're missing Y"). No ability-tier assumption ("at your scale," "for a beginner," "a senior would already know"). No identity-criterion trap (no tourist/practitioner-style contrast at all in this file). Pre-prompt checks are all plausibly-failable for this audience: the extract-prompt's "confirm the folder contains lectures/, exercises/..." verifies a real tar-extraction outcome; the readiness-prompt's "tests run, git status clean, PR possible" verifies genuinely variable per-student repo state. The maintainer block's own accept-note (L86) explicitly applies this exact diagnostic to justify DROPPING the licence/network checks as non-plausibly-failable at this point — the file already practises what the rule asks.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Module abbreviation (2b): body uses full "Module 1" / "Module 2" throughout (L1 title, L7, L60, L76, L80, L82; blockquote L5) — correct for a prework/M1-era file, never bare "M1"/"M2". Term-earning: no curriculum load-bearing term (compounding, the loop, the move, the practice) appears. Claude Code primitives (`/model`, thinking-effort, Session widget, Plan mode, AskUserQuestion) are used without a primer — see the writing §14 row for the reasoning: treated as consistent assumed-known platform vocabulary for this audience, not curriculum-taught concepts being introduced.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — recovery boundary.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Two recovery branches survive in body, both matching the rule's own compliant shape: L34's fallback-repo pointer ("Ask your trainer for the fallback repo, or build one from zero") is the rule text's own named precedent case; L66's "if the agent's screening feels like everything-at-once" branch is a plausible-failure + non-obvious-rescue pair (switch to AskUserQuestion or one-at-a-time) that a student would not otherwise find, and it fires while the session is live — exactly the time-critical-rescue case the rule protects.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.
rules_evaluated.evidence: None of the four prompts append a trailing output-shape spec. Each ends with a plain destination/report ask ("Report the file's size," "Report success on each step and tell me what you did"), matching the ask+destination default.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't ask student to manually diff or spot-check Claude's output as error-catching.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No manual-diff/spot-check instruction anywhere — every confirmation (extraction succeeded, repo is test/branch/commit/PR-ready) is delegated to the agent inside the prompt fence, never handed to the student as a by-hand check. L62 and L66 both name actor+mechanism cleanly ("push back if it dumps all four criteria at once" — actor=you, mechanism=push back, tell=dumping all four at once vs one at a time) and are executable with a visible pass/fail (student can tell whether the agent asked one bug at a time or all four).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No "What research says" callout boxes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No such callout box in this file; the one external citation (Willison, L76) is a plain one-line inline pre-read reference, not a boxed research callout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student moves stay in conversation with agent.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The primary path for every step is an agent prompt (download, extract, install, screen, confirm) — the student never edits a file or runs a terminal command directly. L49's manual-browser-download is an explicitly secondary transport fallback (matches the maintainer's own framing at L105: "the manual-download fallback is a transport primitive, not a file-edit"), not the exercise's forcing function, so it does not trip the practitioner-primitive-at-Debrief-only constraint.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No em-dashes. Simple sentences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: body-view grep `em_dash` 0 hits. Sentences run short-to-moderate throughout; no compound em-dash sub-clauses to split.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Section headers use command verbs when section is about doing something.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Bring real work" / "Pick THE repo" / "Open a Claude Code session" / "Get the content folder" / "Extract the bundle and install" / "Pick a trivial bug and confirm" / "Bring to Module 1" all lead with a command verb correctly. "## Pre-read before Module 1" is the one header that does not (it is a noun label, "Pre-read," not an imperative like "Read before Module 1"), and it is not on rule 17's own canonical-exemption list. Flagged as a rule question rather than a body defect below.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: This is likely a gap in the exempt list rather than a body defect: `check_student_facing.md §33` already treats "Pre-read(s) before Module N" as an established, repeated AE101 header convention (it discusses three such sections by that exact name without objecting to the phrasing). If the maintainer wants strict compliance, rename to "Read before Module 1"; if the convention is intended to stand, add it to rule 17's canonical-exemption list alongside the other architecture-mandated section names.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Inline links use target's title, never filename.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The one internal cross-doc link (L34, "[build one from zero](trainings/agentic-engineering-101/supplementary/build-a-project-from-zero.md)") uses a sentence-case paraphrase of the target's actual H1 ("# No repo to bring? Build one."), not a filename or code-span path. External links (L49 cohort URL, L76 Willison article) are outside this rule's scope (internal curriculum cross-references). No ordinal-as-address usage in body ("Step 4," "the third bullet") — the numbered headers are a sequence label, not a prose cross-reference, and the one place a step-number cross-reference could have leaked ("the skills install in Step 4") sits only in the maintainer block (L106), exempt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguate shared-word collisions with Claude Code primitives on first authored use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Skills" (L7, L22, header 4) refers only to installing pre-built curated skills, never to authoring a team-kit skill — no collision created, no disambiguation owed. "Rules and memory" (L26, L29, L32) is anticipatory framing ("you're going to grow rules and memory here"), not the actual first authored write (that happens in M1), so the first-authored-write trigger has not fired yet. The one deictic present ("lands here," L32) resolves unambiguously to "the repo you just picked" from the same sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: "The agent" is used for autonomous multi-step action (L53 "the agent needs to write outside the repo," L58 "the agent walks three trivial bug candidates," L62 "when the agent gets to the bug screen"). "Claude" is used for invocation/addressee and product/UI reference (L22 "Make sure your Claude Code can operate the GitHub CLI," L45 "Ask Claude to download," L66 "ask Claude to use the AskUserQuestion tool," L82 "Claude Code trick"). No case of the two being swapped; the split matches the active-stance override correctly (autonomous screening/confirming = agent; plain service asks = Claude).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Session / task / run split (all trainings).
rules_evaluated.evidence: "Session" used correctly throughout (L36 header, L38 Session widget, L40 "Open a new Claude Code session"). "Task" used for the work item (L11 "different task sizes"). Noun-"run" as a stand-in for the agent's sitting does not appear anywhere in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No time-of-day anchors in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No tomorrow/overnight/this morning/tonight/next morning/yesterday/last night anywhere in body. The one dated verification note (Windows shell, "verified 2026-08-02") sits below the maintainer cut, exempt.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats stay invisible in flow.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No self-aware pedagogy header or sentence-form contemplative-pause prefix present (no "Pause before you promote," "Meta-moment," "sit with X," "let it land," "take a moment to," "breathe").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cut NVA: true but not moving student forward.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read every bullet and paragraph against "does this change what the student does or notices next?" No administrative asides, no implementation detail stated before its point of use, no obvious-to-a-working-engineer filler. L51-53's permission-mechanics sentence earns its place because it explains an otherwise-confusing prompt behaviour (why approval prompts will fire) rather than restating something obvious.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forward-callout closer: student as grammatical subject.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L80-82's "Bring to Module 1" closers keep the student as subject ("you'll be scrambling," "Bring one") — no training/curriculum-as-subject value-prop leak, no bare imperative coach-register ("watch for X"), no role-gating. L82's "The opening question at Module 1 is X" is a factual heads-up about what happens at the next session's start, not a training-praise or coaching admonition.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework IS the default-setting surface this rule requires (L3-5's blockquote states the `/model` and thinking-effort defaults); the rule's obligation is on each LATER module to restate them at moment of use, which is out of this file's scope.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No act-verb framing around quoted message content anywhere in body (`typing `, `type in`, `say to Claude`, `tell it to` — 0 hits). No literal-trigger-string case to check against the 2026-09-03 carve-outs either (no "say X" construction present at all).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L22 — "Make sure your Claude Code can operate the GitHub CLI. Ask it to install `gh` if it isn't there." — matches the rule's own worked example almost verbatim (state the outcome; hand setup to the agent if it can do it), rather than writing out an auth-flow recipe. Re-checked 32a (2026-09-04, brand new): body does surface `/model` and the "high"/"xhigh"/"medium" thinking-effort labels (L3-5). These read as training-prescribed default OPERATING PARAMETERS the curriculum itself sets (which model and effort level to run each module on), not a discoverable feature-switch a professional is being spared the trouble of finding — the examples the rule gives (an experimental env var, a settings.json key, a permission-mode toggle) are opt-in advanced configuration, structurally different from the mandatory default the whole training runs on. Reading the harm the rule targets (clutter/condescension around a switch nobody needs told), it does not fire on prescriptive session defaults the curriculum requires the student to set.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If the maintainer wants 32a read more literally (any settings name at all, regardless of who is prescribing it), the fix is to move the model/thinking-effort defaults below the maintainer cut and link the docs page — but note this would remove information the training genuinely needs communicated somewhere in body, since it is the training's own operating parameter, not a switch the student discovers on their own.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No sentence whose subject is a module/the training/an exercise/the arc (arc-positioning). The one pre-read annotation (L76) describes what the reading IS ABOUT ("Willison draws the line between vibe coding and working with coding agents as an accountable engineer"), not which later module cashes it in — passing the specific 2026-08-23 carve-out narrowing that "## Pre-reads" sections must clear on their own merits.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The content bundle and curated skills are trainer-authored artefacts the student would not produce themselves (matches the rule's own stated exception) — this is the sanctioned scaffold use, not a violation. Everything the student DOES produce (repo choice, chosen bug, readiness state) is produced through conversation, never unzipped.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is overwhelmingly a setup/launch sequence (pick repo, open session, download, extract, confirm readiness) — mood-floor-exempt per the sibling setup-beat diagnostic (could this be compressed into a parenthetical without breaking the arc? yes, it is plumbing). The one interactive move (bug-screen push-back) leaves the student in quiet operational confidence, consistent with priming the arc's opening earned-trust register at M1 without pre-empting it. No signature wrong-edit for a setup beat (no verification/resolving-doubt content masquerading as a teaching moment).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt A contains the literal `<CONTENT_URL>` placeholder inside the fence, which would otherwise violate this rule outright. The maintainer block (below the cut) documents an explicit, named exception: "`<CONTENT_URL>`: literal placeholder in source, build-time substituted per-customer by `scripts/build-workbook.js`. Explicit exception to `check_prompts.md §1`... covered by build substitution, not student fill-in." This is a documented accept-note, not a body defect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt A (L45, download), Prompt B (§2c-exempt, permission-mechanics paragraph only, matches the rule's own calibration example naming THIS file's §4), and Prompt D (L66, "ask Claude to use the AskUserQuestion tool...") all carry a correct, proportionate lead-in. Prompt C (screen-and-ready, under header "## 5. Pick a trivial bug and confirm Module 1 readiness") does not: the text immediately before the fence (L62, "When the agent gets to the bug screen, push back if it dumps all four criteria at once...") is push-back guidance for AFTER the prompt runs, not a semantic-summary lead-in of what the prompt does. The closer semantic-summary sentence sits one paragraph earlier (L58, "The agent walks three trivial bug candidates... helps you pick one, then confirms...") and is phrased in third person about the agent rather than as an imperative "Ask Claude to..." lead-in.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Minor, non-blocking: either fold a one-clause "Ask Claude to screen three candidates and confirm readiness" onto the push-back paragraph immediately before the fence, or accept that the header + first paragraph together already discharge §2c's intent and the second paragraph is legitimately a distinct move (push-back coaching), not a missing lead-in.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four prompts use the exact `**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*` label with no `copy →` prefix and no `(end of prompt)` closer. Each prompt's own text names its expected return shape inline ("Report the file's size," "Report success on each step and tell me what you did"), so a separate after-fence return-shape line is not needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt B's step 2 references `~/Downloads/ae101-content.tar.gz`, the exact deterministic path Prompt A wrote to — no invented alias, no fuzzy fallback needed since both ends use the same literal path.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This rule targets planner→grill-style exercise chains that stage a deliberate contrast (a later prompt must not be pre-told what an earlier prompt is meant to discover). Prework's prompts are mechanical setup steps (download, extract, screen, confirm) with no such staged-discovery pipeline; nothing here has a "grill is next" concern to leak.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: none of the four prompts use `**bold**` or `*italic*` inside the fence. Prompt B uses plain numbered steps and plain bullets; backticks used only for paths/filenames.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Question-dump default — `in turn` too soft; two legal shapes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts B and C use "ask one question at a time if you need to, no preamble" — softer than shape (a)'s full "wait for my answer... DO NOT show me the next question," but the file pairs this with a built-in shape-(b) remediation almost verbatim to the rule's own worked example: Prompt D + its L66 lead-in ("ask Claude to use the AskUserQuestion tool, or to give you the candidate-bug screen one bug at a time. Whichever reads better.") is a body callout handing the student the choice, exactly matching "Use the AskUserQuestion tool, or ask the agent to give you findings one at a time if you'd rather. Your call." The softer initial phrasing plus explicit designed recovery reads as deliberate: this is prework's own first push-back teaching moment (learning to catch and correct a batching agent), not an oversight the prompt should have engineered away.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Preamble before action — design around it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Not plan mode — the 2026-09-03 narrowing makes this rule advisory-only here, and Prompts B and C already include "no preamble" as a suppressor clause proactively, beyond what is required.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four prompts favour post-action reporting over pre-confirm: Prompt A "Report the file's size," Prompt B and C both close "Report success on each step and tell me what you did." None of the actions (local filesystem writes, a bug screening conversation) are irreversible/external-trust-line actions that would need the pre-confirm carve-out.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt B's absolute paths (`~/Documents/ae101-content`, `~/Downloads/ae101-content.tar.gz`) are not the session's own working directory (the picked repo) — they are distinct target locations OUTSIDE the repo, which the exercise genuinely needs named explicitly (matches the rule's own carve-out: naming the path is the action when the intent is to write elsewhere).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: all four labels are exactly `**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*`, matching `expandPrompts`' reconstruction from registry frontmatter.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four prompts open with a direct, concrete ask (download this file / walk these three steps / screen three bugs / use this tool) built from state the body already established (repo picked, tarball location, criteria given) — none opens with "ask me which..." orchestration bloat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mechanical: body contains four `{{prompt:...}}` markers (L47, L55, L64, L68 in raw source), no inline fenced prompt blocks. Keys follow the `<training>-<module>-<verb-noun>` naming convention (`ae101-prework-download-tarball`, `ae101-prework-extract-and-install`, `ae101-prework-screen-and-ready`, `ae101-prework-one-at-a-time`).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read each prompt in isolation: Prompt A carries its own 401-retry logic and full URL; Prompt B names the exact default path and asks Claude to find the OS-appropriate skills location itself rather than hard-coding one; Prompt C and D rely only on same-session cwd/scrollback, which the session-boundary check (rule 40, below) confirms is warm and safe to assume.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt A splits its three moves (download+report / auth-wall handling / URL) into three paragraphs. Prompt B and C use numbered lists, one move per number. Prompt D is a single short sentence under the ≤30-word/≤2-move threshold and correctly stays one paragraph.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompt A: lead-in verb "download" mirrors prompt opening "Download," noun-phrases close enough (filename/folder named in both, just split slightly differently). Prompt B: §2c makes this vacuous (no lead-in exists by design). Prompt D: strong mirror ("ask Claude to use the AskUserQuestion tool" ↔ "Use the AskUserQuestion tool... One candidate at a time"). Prompt C is the exception: its nearest lead-in-shaped sentence ("The agent walks three trivial bug candidates... helps you pick one, then confirms...") does not share verb or noun-phrase with the prompt's actual opening ("Walk these in order, ask one question at a time if you need to, no preamble"). Same underlying passage as the §2 row above.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Same fix as §2: tighten the paragraph immediately before the fence so its opening clause mirrors the prompt's own opening ("Walk these in order..."), or accept the header+first-paragraph pairing as sufficient and treat this as a rule-boundary question rather than a defect.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Session opens fresh at L36-40 ("Open a new Claude Code session at the repo you just picked") and stays warm through every subsequent prompt (no `/clear`, no cwd change, no sub-task boundary between steps 3-5). Prompt B's references are deterministic paths anyway (safe even if read cold). Prompt C's "this repo" resolves via the agent's own cwd, not a curriculum-coined label. Prompt D's "screening" is grounded in Prompt C's own literal prior text ("Screen against:"), satisfying 40b's requirement that a referenced term must have appeared in a prior PROMPT, not just body prose. No parallel-worktree corollary (40a) applies — single session throughout.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A leading-looking line can be a forcing function; prefer the simpler prompt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is an edit-time diagnostic for fix passes on an existing prompt. No edit is under review here, and none of the four prompts show gratuitous added structure or a stripped load-bearing leading line to weigh against the simpler alternative.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A take-home prompt asks for one bounded build.
rules_evaluated.evidence: None of the four prompts are take-home/handoff prompts saved and run in a later, unattended session — all four run synchronously within the same guided prework session.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood contract named.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prework is a setup/orientation beat (repo pick, session open, content download, bug screen) that precedes the arc's taught-mood sequence. Mood-floor is exempt for setup/launch beats per this rule's own diagnostic (could the beat compress into a parenthetical without breaking the arc? yes — it is logistics). One sentence stating what the student leaves this piece in: quiet operational readiness — I know what to bring and what to do — which sets up M1's earned-trust opening without resolving or pre-empting it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.

Nothing in this file's content contradicts that clearance on a fresh read: the Plan Mode / push-back mentions stay at the sizing/interaction level, not a full teach, leaving M3's and earn-the-trust's own teaching moments intact.
